defects.summary: Decompression bomb (CWE-409) in the offline-import extraction path: plugin.packager.unpack (packager.py:185) does atomic_write_bytes(target, zf.read(info)) with no max_length, fully decompressing each member into memory and writing it whole to disk with no per-member or total uncompressed-size cap. plugin.lifecycle.install's free-space preflight (lifecycle.py:299) checks only the COMPRESSED archive size, and _verify_staged runs AFTER extraction, so a small crafted package that expands to many GB causes memory/disk exhaustion during install of an untrusted package. Measured 64 MiB member from 65,232 B (ratio 1028.8:1) drove unpack peak-memory to 148,453,193 B and wrote 67,108,864 B. Not a path escape and not code exec; the transactional journal rmtree's staging on failure, so impact is a transient install-time DoS. Fix: cap cumulative and per-member uncompressed size (compare zi.file_size against a budget; stream zf.open(info) with a bounded read) before writing.

report.question: Does the install/import path accept an archive containing ../ traversal entries, absolute paths, symlinks pointing outside the extraction root, or a Windows device name - and where does each land?
report.answer: NO for every path-hostile vector. Relative traversal, absolute, drive-absolute and UNC members are refused with PluginError E_IO by check_relpath before any byte is written (0 escapes); Windows device names (nul/con/aux/com*/lpt*, incl. dotted/nested) are refused the same clean way on the real win32 target (handled, not a crash); a symlink member is written as a CONTAINED REGULAR FILE (unpack reads content, never calls os.symlink) so no external symlink exists; ZIP has no hardlink member type. Nothing lands outside the destination root. Defense is layered: a pre-normalisation string check (check_relpath) AND a post-normalisation containment check (safe_join's os.path.abspath + relative_to), applied per member. The ONE real exposure is orthogonal to path-hostility: the compression-ratio member is decompressed with NO uncompressed-size cap (zf.read has no max_length; preflight sizes only the compressed archive) -> a decompression-bomb DoS on offline import (P2).
